name: End of the World

gist.Armageddon: Hits every target on the board, its caster included, and ends the turn. If no hero is left standing afterwards, the player with more creatures wins.
gist.Ifrit: Each Ifrit makes every Armageddon hit much harder; Ifrits are untouched by Armageddon.
gist.Damus, the Prophet of Apocalypse: Places an Ifrit each turn for free; his Ifrits take no damage from your cards; Armageddon gets cheaper per Ifrit, and with an Ifrit out he is untouched by it.
gist.Pseudonia, the Skill Devourer: Very sturdy; permanently gains the effect of each hero that is defeated.
gist.Kazena, the Storming Rebel: Once per turn draws back up to seven.
gist.Cloud Pillow: Halves the damage one of its targets takes until its next turn; used before its own Armageddon.
gist.Book of Doom: Pays gold to hit any number of targets lightly.
gist.Pure Advantage Camel: Trap creature; also a body for the tie-break.
gist.Cactus Creature: Trap creature that moves a status onto another target.
gist.Noble Mummy Guards: Trap creature that returns one of your Abilities to hand.
gist.Frolake: Draws on arrival and refills the hand at end of turn.

plan: It counts down to one spell. Damus places Ifrits; each makes Armageddon stronger and cheaper, his Ifrits ignore your damage, and with one of them out he himself is untouched by the blast. Two or three Ifrits in, Armageddon flattens every hero on the table except Damus, and if nobody is left at all the player with more creatures wins, which against a creatureless deck is always this one. Until then it stalls with trap creatures, Cloud Pillows and Book of Doom. Everything depends on Damus being active and on the Ifrits, which shrug off damage but not theft or removal.

looks.early: Damus with one Ifrit, a few face-down creatures, Wealth.
looks.mid: Three Ifrits, an Armageddon searched and waiting, its other heroes on Cloud Pillows.
looks.late: The table levelled; Damus and his Ifrits standing in the smoke.

opening.tell: Damus places an Ifrit every turn; your damage does nothing to them.
opening.why: The Ifrits cannot be burned, but Damus can, and the whole deck is his text box.

midgame.tell: Two Ifrits stand beside Damus and he has searched an Armageddon.
midgame.why: Each Ifrit removed makes the blast weaker and dearer, and The Yeeting and Dark Gear are not damage; a stolen Ifrit even gives you a creature for the tie-break.

crisis.tell: Armageddon is coming next turn and your heroes are already hurt.
crisis.why: The blast hits everything at once, and only heroes with enough health or a shield survive it: heal, put Cloud in a Bottle and Homerun! on the right heroes, and do not spend the turn attacking.

endgame.tell: Both sides are low, and it controls creatures while you control none.
endgame.why: If one more Armageddon leaves nobody standing, the side with more creatures wins: either Damus dies before it is cast or you hold a stolen creature when it is.

opening.board: Damus sets an Ifrit beside himself; your burn slides off it.

options.text: Snow Cannon Damus: frozen, his Ifrits can be hurt

opening.board: A Camel and a Frolake appear; it is in no hurry.

options.text: White Eye it out of the hand

midgame.board: Cloud Pillows go onto its other two heroes.
Noble Mummy Guards bounces your Destruction Magic.

options.text: Burn Damus with what you have
Heal, Cloud in a Bottle, Homerun! in hand
Remove an Ifrit to shrink it

crisis.board: The blast lands: everything but Damus and the Ifrits is hit very hard, and its turn ends.

options.text: Heal first, then finish its wounded heroes
Its own heroes took it: finish them
Kill Damus before it is cast

endgame.board: One hero each, both low; it has two creatures, you have none.

options.text: Steal a creature, or kill Damus first

endgame.board: Damus is gone; the Ifrits can be hurt and Armageddon would hit its own side.

options.text: Still steal an Ifrit for the tie-break

endgame.board: Pseudonia has inherited a fallen hero's effect.
